thread:
maria: Quick thread - fintech customer asked about month-end reliability. They want short high-magnitude bursts (5-7x) for a 90-120m window. Sales pushed back on full reserved pools pricing. Suggest we prototype a 'buffered-commit' product: escrowed short-term tokens + elastic prewarm handshake. Thoughts?

jordan: Buffered-commit sounds clearer than 'smoothing'. what's the consumer contract? guaranteed? best-effort?

maria: baseline guarantee remains reserved baseline. buffered tokens are sold as an amortized buffer that can be consumed during a declared peak window. We call it "escrowed burst credits". Contract: guaranteed baseline + escrowed credits best-effort with defined fallback behavior and a premium over baseline for consumed credits.

sam: fallback behavior is critical. Need deterministic variant fallback and throttling rules so customers know quality won't unexpectedly change.

kai: infra angle: we need a short reservation handshake so autoscaler can pre-warm. Proposed flow: customer signals planned peak (start+duration, expected rps multiplier) -> control-plane mints ephemeral escrow token -> routing attaches token to requests -> scheduler uses token weight to pre-warm nodes. Token has TTL and consumption meter.

ashley: billing: how do we charge? two parts: amortized escrow fee (monthly) + consumed-credit surcharge. Show cost estimator in console. Also need clear invoice lines for accounting teams.

rachel: legal/SLA folks will want explicit failure modes. can we define disqualifying conditions? e.g., force-majors, cross-tenant event where cluster budget exhausted.

maria: yes. propose explicit rollback triggers: 1) cluster-level CPU oversubscription > 12% sustained for 10m; 2) non-escrow tenant p95 latency regressions > 15% for 5m; 3) autoscaler prewarm miss rate > 20% for 10m. If triggers fire, new escrow grants are paused and existing customers downgraded to best-effort without prewarm.

jordan: metrics we need: escrow.active_tokens, escrow.bytes_consumed, escrow.prewarm_hit_rate, escrow.impact_non_escrow_p95, escrow.cluster_budget_usage. Also correlate with model_variant_fallback events.

sam: scheduling detail: token RSVP weight should be translated to a soft reservation (not pinned pods) so we don't overcommit. Maybe a multi-tier token: RSVP-high (explicit prewarm), RSVP-low (no prewarm, cheaper).

kai: good idea. config sketch for infra teams (for discussion):

```
# buffered-commit policy
policy_name: buffered_commit_v1
baseline_rps: "80"
escrow_multiplier_options: ["3","5","7"]
burst_window_seconds: "5400"  # 90m default
token_ttl_seconds: "600"
prewarm_tiers:
  - name: RSVP-high
    prewarm: true
    weight: 3
    cost_multiplier: 1.4
  - name: RSVP-low
    prewarm: false
    weight: 1
    cost_multiplier: 1.0
tenant_cap_per_cluster: "2500"
cluster_escrow_pct: "0.10"
```

ashley: launch criteria (draft):
- infra: prewarm success rate >= 92% for RSVP-high tokens during staging load tests
- infra: no >10% p95 regression for non-escrow tenants in staging
- product: pilot signed with 2 customers (one steady high baseline, one spiky)
- billing: invoicing line item validated and estimated cost calculator in console
- security: KMS audit for escrow token issuance

maria: rollback conditions reiterated above. add canary rollout: start with 0.5% of traffic on a single region, ramp to 2% then 10% over two weeks if metrics stable.

rachel: ops: make sure we have a fast kill switch for region-level disable and a per-tenant throttle override. Also add chaos test: simultaneous RSVPs from 40 tenants to test enforcement.

sam: runtime: need token enforcement in admission path + token metering in request plane. Also integrate with model-routing table so variant fallback mapping is deterministic and logged.

jordan: product docs should include decision trees for sales: when to sell reserved pool vs buffered-commit vs no-commit. Need ROI calc for customer.

maria: owners and next steps:
- product: finalize buffered-commit contract language & pilot pricing (owner: maria)
- infra: implement RSVP token prototype + prewarm scheduler hooks on staging (owner: kai)
- runtime: admission enforcement + deterministic fallback mapping (owner: sam)
- billing: invoice format & amortization model (owner: ashley)
- legal/ops: SLA failure modes & kill-switch design (owner: rachel)
- qa: chaos test plan + canary harness (owner: kai)

maria: timeline goal: prototype in 10 business days, internal dogfood in 4 weeks, pilot start in 10 weeks.

jordan: i'll be primary eng liaison for runtime changes.

ops-bot: Reminder: Create #buffered-commit-proto channel and schedule weekly sync.

kai: will add a staging job to simulate RSVPs and report prewarm hit-rate.

ashley: i'll draft the console estimator mock and share with product for feedback.

maria: one last note - make sure refund/credit policy is clear if prewarm fails. we'll propose pro-rata credits for unmet escrowed credits.

jordan: agree. ok to proceed with prototyping.

maria: thanks team, i'll post the PRD update and the short sales one-pager later today.
